claims.basis: The period Motor Sport history identifies the V12 250F development, its 250F chassis application and the five-speed transaxle; the AC package explicitly names the twelve-cylinder variant.

The source explicitly states the V12 was mated to a five-speed transaxle. The 250F is a driver-operated manual transaxle with a period lever layout; the reviewed photos do not expose a legible gate, so confidence is deliberately low. The 250F family has a physical clutch and driver-operated manual transmission; the V12 retained the 250F chassis control arrangement. Manual blip is modeled as a downshift action. Automatic blip is modeled as a downshift action. Throttle lift is modeled for upshift technique here. No downshift cut action is documented. The V12 photograph and the full-resolution 250F cockpit image show the conventional large wooden round rim. The inspected wheel carries no display; gauges are separate. No wheel-mounted shift lights are visible. The photographed conventional rim is closed and continuous.
